correctness.rationale: Proved binary scaling P_(2^k d)=P_d via t(2^k q+s)=t(q) xor t(s), and global complement closure via adding a new high leading bit. For odd d, a 192-state carry+parity transducer tracks x+jd for j=1,2,3, with carry bounds c_j<=j. Higher zero bits of d plus guessed bits of starting n are handled by exact reverse reachability, not finite prefixes. Independently reimplemented both transitions and subset determinization without using the source verifier: precisely 195 reachable subsets after initial odd bit, with output masks 0x6e (5), 0xf7 (6), 0xff (184); zero cycles and all one-bit edges establish A only d=1, B only d=3, C all other odd d. Corresponding relative-mask sizes 5,7,8; complement gives 10,14,16. Checker addresses all unbounded input words because finite reachable graph is exhausted. Supplemental finite prefix computations are not infinite proof.
residual_risks: Only length-four binary Thue--Morse arithmetic factors; does not compute minimal occurrence positions or lengths >=5.

originality.rationale: Joshi--Rust's automata theorem gives length>=4 monochromatic arithmetic progressions for each difference with odd part>1, but no nonmonochromatic four-word spectrum. Aedo et al. study maximum monochromatic runs and their arithmetic scaling, while Avgustinovich--Fon-Der-Flaass--Frid study union-over-d arithmetical complexity. The fixed-difference 14-versus-16 separation at d odd-part3 is not implied by any of these statements. The 2003 primary complete work remains unread.
